violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw eggs were stored over produce and ready to eat foods in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The PIC moved the eggs during the inspection to correct. The EHS educated the PIC on how to properly stored raw foods and provided a fact sheet to the PIC.

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: When asked how the equipment and utensils are sanitized, the PIC said they aren’t.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. The EHS explained the importance of and the requirement of cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils. The EHS told the PIC how to properly set up and use the 3-compartment sink,

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: chicken, pork belly and pupusas in the countertop hot holding unit were not being held hot enough at 115º, 112º, and 106ºF.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. The ambient temperature of the unit was set to 28ºC (82ºF), which is not hot enough to keep foods 135ºF and above as required. The foods were prepared at 9:30 and today. The PIC stated they will be served by 1:00 pm today. If not served, the food must be discarded. The PIC turned up the holding temperature of the unit. Ensure hot foods are held at 135º F at all times.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Cole slaw and cut lettuce were not being held cold enough on the ice bath due to the ice level being too low. Cole slaw was 45º and lettuce was 43º. Black beans cooked yesterday were 50ºF in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The PIC adjusted the ice level during the inspection to cool the foods down. The black beans were not cold enough due to not being properly cooled. The beans were discarded due to temperature abuse. The EHS educated the PIC on how to properly cool large quantities of cooked foods and provided the employee with a fact sheet/handout explaining it.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: A large container of black beans cooked yesterday were not cooled properly due to too much food in the container and the container being covered.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. The EHS explained to the PIC how to properly cool large quantities of cooked foods. The black beans were discarded.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Handled Single-Service/Use Items Storage
violations.observation: The handles of the plastic forks, spoons and knives were not dispensed so that touching food contact surfaces could be avoided.
violations.corrective_action: Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by employees and consumers if consumer self- service is provided. The EHS educated the PIC on how to properly display the utensils with all handles lined up in one direction to avoid contact with the food contact surfaces of the utensils.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed there was a foul odor near the grease trap.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. The PIC stated the grease trap is scheduled to be cleaned today. Clean the grease trap as often as necessary to avoid foul odors. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate in a conspicuous location.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. Post the health permit In a conspicuous location where customers can see it. Correct by the follow up.

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils. Observed an employee drinking coffee from a mug in the food area.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw beef was stored over onions and cabbage in the walking refrigerator. Raw chicken was stored over fresh peppers in the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The manager corrected this by moving the beef to a lower shelf.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: coleslaw, cut, lettuce, and mayonnaise were all 61°F in the cold rail. There were several whole chickens that were cooked yesterday in the walk-in that were 49° 46° and 47°.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All products were discarded due to temperature abuse. The chickens were discarded . CDI.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: observed prepared chicken tacos in the refrigerator an expiration date of 12/17 (9 days ago). There was also a container of salad dressing with an expiration date of 12/11/25.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. This food manager corrected this by discarding the chicken tacos. The salad dressing was discarded.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: there are several foods prepared on site and held more for 24 hours, but not many were being date marked properly.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. All foods prepared on site and held more than 24 hours must be date marked with an expiration date, not to exceed 7 days past the day of it was prepared with the day of preparation, counting as day one. For instance, chicken tacos prepared on December 1 and held more than 24 hours, would need to be marked with an expiration date of December 7. Any chicken tacos left after that date would have to be discarded. Correct by the follow-up on January 5, 2026. LATINO CHICKEN PLACE (Inspection Date: 12/26/2025) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: The certified food manager could not provide a food temperature measuring device. CFM had a food thermometer, but had to leave the kitchen to find it.
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. Keep the food thermometer in the kitchen so that it can be used as needed.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: there were several unlabeled squeeze bottles in the food prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. All food containers must be labeled label all squeeze bottles by follow up.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Insect Control Devices, Installation
violations.observation: Observe two rolls of fly paper hanging from the ceiling over the food prep areas.
violations.corrective_action: Relocate the insect control device so that it is not located over a food preparation area and dead insects are prevented from being falling on exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Remove the fly paper by the follow up.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. Store wet wiping cloths in a sanitizer solution in between uses.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: plastic bowls were being used to dispense ingredients from large ingredient containers, which makes it impossible to not touch the ingredients when dispensing.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Replace the bowls with handled utensils and keep the handles out of the food. LATINO CHICKEN PLACE (Inspection Date: 12/26/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Clean Linens Free of Food Residues/Soil
violations.observation: Clean linens were visibly soiled with food debris. The wiping cloths used for cleaning the food and no food context services were visibly soiled and not clean as required.
violations.corrective_action: Clean linens shall be free from food residues and other soiling matter. Replace the wiping cloth more often and stored them in the sanitizing solution between uses.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Corrosion-Resistant/Nonabsorbent Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not durable: observed a large clear plastic garlic manufacturer container being reused to store food. The container was bulging and deformed, most likely due to hot food being placed in it.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be durable, corrosion-resistant, and nonabsorbent. Manufacturer containers are not designed to be re-used. Discontinue reusing manufacturer containers and discard the garlic container. Use only NSF or equivalent approved equipment. Correct by the follow up.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: folded cardboard boxes were being used a line shelving in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. Folded cardboard boxes are not an approved non-food contact surface. Remove the cardboard boxes by the follow up.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: the shelving in the walk-in refrigerator had significant amount of food debris build up on it
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean the walk-in refrigerator shelving before the follow up.
